passage: Wednesday. At break, I saw Jatin sitting alone under the neem tree with his lunchbox closed. Everyone else was playing. I walked over. “Can I sit with you?” He shrugged, but he made room. I didn't say much. I opened my lunch and offered him a piece of my paratha. After a while, he said, “I miss my old school.” I said, “That sounds hard.” Then a group of boys came by and said something mean about his accent. I stood up and said, “Leave him alone.” They walked away, and I told Mrs. Rao what happened. Jatin looked at me and said thanks. Amandeep.

qa.q: What was Jatin probably feeling when he sat with his lunchbox closed?
qa.a: He was probably lonely and missing his old school, which he said aloud after Amandeep sat with him.

qa.q: What did Amandeep do when the boys said something mean?
qa.a: Amandeep said “Leave him alone” and then told Mrs. Rao, so an adult knew.

qa.q: How might Amandeep have felt when the boys said something mean about Jatin's accent?
qa.a: Amandeep was probably protective of Jatin, standing up to say, "Leave him alone," and then telling Mrs. Rao.

grounding: A child sits with a lonely classmate and stands up for him, showing care, and also involves an adult.

passage: Under the peepal tree at the village school, Farida sat by herself with her knees drawn up, because the girls had left her out of the skipping rope game. Deepika saw her and stopped playing. She came over with two guavas from her bag and sat beside Farida. “Want one?” Farida took it without a word. Deepika ate hers, then said, “Come and jump with me.” Farida shook her head, so Deepika stayed where she was, and the two of them watched the rope from the shade. After a few minutes Farida stood up. “Okay, my turn next,” she said. Deepika grinned.

qa.q: How many guavas did Deepika bring?
What did Deepika's choice to stay beside Farida show about what she wanted?
qa.a: She wanted Farida to feel less alone, and staying without pushing showed care and respect for Farida's feelings.

qa.q: What helped Farida rejoin the game?
qa.a: Deepika sat with her, shared a guava and did not force her, and after a few minutes Farida chose to stand up.

qa.q: How might Farida have felt when the girls left her out?
qa.a: Farida probably felt lonely and hurt, since she sat by herself with her knees drawn up.

grounding: A child sits with a lonely classmate to show care and solidarity, without pressuring her to join.
